1.bug_scenario: The TimePicker component in the React package currently does not honor a “readOnly” prop: when you set readOnly on <TimePicker> the inputs and dropdown arrows remain interactive and are not styled differently. Per the design spec the entire control should remain focusable but not editable: the text fields and selects should render in a read-only background, the arrows should not open the menu, and a new “bx--time-picker--readonly” modifier should apply. Additionally, we need to expose the prop in the docs, add a read-only story, and write RTL tests to verify the class name appears.

2.bug_scenario: When you pass the new readOnly prop into the React TimePicker (e.g. <TimePicker readOnly>…), the component doesn’t render in a read-only style, nor does it block editing or opening its dropdowns. There’s no CSS for a “read-only” state in the SCSS, no support in the component code, no stories or Playground controls, and no RTL tests to verify it. The design docs (screenshots) call for a disabled background, placeholder text color, disabled icons and consistent spacing but none of that is implemented yet.
